title: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Competes on Price, Not Just Power
summary: OpenAI released GPT-5.

title: A Reviewer Flagged Two Papers for Fake Authors. Both Were Accepted Anyway.
summary: A conference reviewer flagged two submitted research papers for having fabricated authors, and both were still accepted as oral presentations — the top tier of acceptance.

title: Google Is Rolling Out Age Checks Across Android Worldwide
summary: Google will extend age verification on Android to every market by the end of the year, using signals from Google Play to tell apps whether a user is an adult.

title: Google's Robots Learn to Use Their Whole Body
summary: DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2, which coordinates a robot's entire body — legs, torso, and arms together — instead of treating the arm as a separate problem from balance and movement.

title: They Gave an AI a Real Business. It Lost $447.
summary: Researchers handed GPT-5.

title: The Honest Number for AI Coding Is 2x, Not 10x
summary: A developer wrote up a year of working with AI coding tools and put the realistic productivity gain at roughly double, not the tenfold figure that circulates in marketing.

title: Stacked Pull Requests Are Now Live on GitHub
summary: GitHub put stacked pull requests into public preview.

title: Idle Chips Are the AI Industry's Grounded Aircraft
summary: A Hugging Face analysis borrows a lesson from aviation: for most of that industry's history, the number that best predicted whether an airline survived was how much of the day each aircraft spent on the ground.

title: Does AI Reasoning Actually Reason?
summary: Quanta Magazine looks at a growing body of research asking whether AI models that show their work are genuinely reasoning, or arriving at right answers for the wrong reasons.

title: A Security Vendor's Post-Mortem on the Hugging Face Break-In
summary: Previously covered on 2026-07-29: Hugging Face published a minute-by-minute account of the July intrusion in which attackers, aided by AI, reached part of its production systems.

title: Microsoft Releases a Charting Language Built for AI Tools
summary: Microsoft published Flint, a language for describing charts that is designed to be written by AI assistants rather than by hand.

title: BMW Puts Movie Advertising on the Dashboard
summary: A consumer rights wiki documented BMW displaying Spider-Man advertising on the screens inside customers' cars.

title: Case-Folding Every Byte of GitHub's Code Search at 45 GiB/s
summary: GitHub's engineering team detailed how it makes code search case-insensitive at scale.

title: Running Kimi K3 in 29 GB of RAM — Very, Very Slowly
summary: A developer released a tool that runs Kimi K3, a large open AI model, on a machine with only 29 GB of memory.

title: Anthropic Releases Claude Opus 5
summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, the newest model in its Opus tier.

title: ByteDance Releases Seedance 2.5
summary: ByteDance published Seedance 2.

title: China Starts Making Its Own Advanced Chipmaking Machines
summary: China has begun producing home-grown immersion deep-ultraviolet lithography machines — the equipment that prints circuits onto silicon — according to a source cited by Reuters.

title: AI Financial Advice Holds Up Better Than Expected
summary: MIT Sloan looked at how well AI assistants answer personal finance questions and found the advice largely holds up — provided you ask specific questions rather than vague ones.

title: US Warns of Attacks on Water Utility Controllers
summary: CISA, the US cybersecurity agency, issued an alert about attackers targeting the programmable controllers that run water treatment and distribution equipment.

title: TLS 1.2's Oldest Key Exchange Methods Are Officially Deprecated
summary: The IETF published RFC 10015, which formally deprecates obsolete key exchange methods in TLS 1.

title: A Soundness Bug in Lean's Proof Kernel, Written Up in Full
summary: Leonardo de Moura published a postmortem for bug #14576 in the kernel of Lean, the proof assistant — the small trusted core that checks every proof the system accepts.

title: Alibaba's Qwen Team Releases Qwen3.8-Max
summary: Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen3.

title: Californians Can Now Force Data Brokers to Delete Their Data
summary: California's DROP system — one request that reaches the data brokers holding your personal information — became enforceable on August 1.

title: A Working Example of GitHub's Stacked Pull Requests
summary: Previously covered on 2026-07-31: GitHub put stacked pull requests — splitting one large change into a chain of smaller reviewable pieces — into public preview.

title: Why People Get Attached to Their Tools
summary: Stack Overflow published an argument that developers cling to particular tools because a tool people have used for years encodes trust — you know exactly how it behaves when things go wrong.

title: Thinking Machines Publishes a Model Called Inkling
summary: The AI lab Thinking Machines released a model named Inkling on Hugging Face, the site where open models are shared and downloaded.

title: Dependabot Now Waits Three Days Before Suggesting an Update
summary: Dependabot is the GitHub service that automatically opens a pull request when a piece of third-party code your project depends on publishes a new version.

title: A Language Model Running on a 6502
summary: A developer got an autoregressive language model — the same basic design as the chatbots you use, generating one word at a time and feeding each one back in — running on the 6502, the 8-bit processor from the 1970s that powered the Apple II, the Commodore 64 and the NES.

title: OpenAI Publishes Ten New Results in Mathematics and Computer Science
summary: OpenAI published a list of ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science that its models contributed to.

title: A Large AI Model Now Fits on a Laptop — and a Smaller One on Your Phone
summary: A developer released Swiftlet, an open-source tool that runs Qwen, an 80-billion-parameter AI model, in 4.

title: AI Helps Experts More Than It Helps Beginners
summary: Engineer Sean Goedecke argues that large language models pay off in proportion to what you already know: an expert spots the wrong answer and redirects, while a novice takes it at face value.

title: A New Video Model Arrives With Sound Built In
summary: MiniMax released H3, a video generation model with openly published weights, native audio, and output up to 2K resolution — and it works in ComfyUI, a popular free tool for building image and video pipelines, from day one.

title: A Benchmark for Whether Voice AI Actually Sounds Human
summary: Hugging Face published Real World VoiceEQ, a way of measuring the human quality of voice AI rather than just its accuracy.

title: Cloudflare on Serving Open Models at Scale
summary: Cloudflare wrote up how it runs Kimi and GLM — two large open-weight models — across its network, covering the compression work that shrinks them, the changes that cut response time, and the guardrails around what they output.

title: Why Routing Between AI Models Is Harder Than It Looks
summary: IBM Research published a piece on model routing — automatically sending each request to the cheapest model that can handle it, and escalating to a stronger one only when needed.

title: GitHub's Legal Team Built Its Own Tools — Without Writing Code
summary: GitHub published an account of how its own legal team used Copilot CLI, a command-line AI assistant, to build small tools that automate parts of their day-to-day work.

title: A Browser Flaw Is Leaking the Addresses iCloud Private Relay Hides
summary: Security researchers at Mysk found that WebKit, the engine behind Safari and every browser on iPhone, leaks your real IP address and the sites you look up, even when you are using a proxy or Apple's iCloud Private Relay.

title: Mistral Releases a Free Model for Spotting Harmful Content
summary: The French AI company Mistral released Shieldstral, a small open model that reviews both text and images and flags content that breaks safety rules.

title: Interpol Says AI Now Drives Most Cybercrime in Africa
summary: Interpol reported that more than half of cybercrime across Africa is now powered by AI, as automated scams surge.

title: Flowise, a Popular Drag-and-Drop AI Builder, Is Shutting Down
summary: Flowise, one of the better-known tools for assembling AI workflows by dragging boxes around instead of coding, announced it is sunsetting.

title: An Active Supply Chain Attack Has Compromised Keyv and Its Neighbours
summary: Security firm Aikido reported that Keyv — a widely used npm package for caching data, pulled in indirectly by a great many JavaScript projects — has been compromised as part of the ongoing Shai-Hulud campaign.

title: Liquid AI Ships a 2.6-Billion-Parameter Agent That Runs on the Device Itself
summary: Previously covered on 2026-07-29: Liquid AI released the LFM2.

title: Google DeepMind Changes Hands at the Top
summary: Google announced that Demis Hassabis, who co-founded DeepMind and has led it as CEO, is moving to the role of Chair, and that Jeff Dean is leaving the company.

title: Nashville Votes to Seize Land to Stop a Data Centre
summary: Nashville's council approved an eminent domain action to halt a data centre project planned near the city zoo.

title: Atlassian's AI Assistant Can Be Talked Into Leaking Company Data
summary: Security researchers at PromptArmor showed that Rovo, the AI assistant built into Atlassian's Jira and Confluence, can be made to pull information out of a workspace and send it elsewhere — getting around the permission controls that are supposed to stop exactly that.

title: Cloudflare Announces an Operating System for AI Agents
summary: Cloudflare introduced Cloudflare OS, which it describes as an open platform for running agents, apps and work on its network.

title: Why the AI Scores in Every Press Release Keep Losing Meaning
summary: A piece in Communications of the ACM applies Goodhart's law to AI benchmarks: once a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure.

title: Open Models Beat a Frontier Model at Retrieval, for 1/100th the Cost
summary: Neon published results for Castform, its retrieval setup — the step where a system searches your documents for the passages relevant to a question before an AI model answers.

title: Removing a Single 'if' Made a Filter Four Times Faster
summary: A Rust developer walked through speeding up a filtering routine by 4x, and the change was to delete an if-statement rather than add cleverness.

title: People Approving AI Actions Miss One Dangerous Request in Three
summary: A study across 40,000 simulated runs found that when people were shown what an AI agent wanted to do and asked to approve or deny it, they missed roughly one in three harmful commands.

title: Meta Ordered to Pay $942 Million Over Harm to Children
summary: A court ordered Meta to pay $942 million to address harm caused to children by its social media products.

title: A Reporter Was Stalked Through a Child's Smartwatch
summary: Wired documented how hackers took over a smartwatch marketed for children and used it to track a person's movements and listen in.

title: OpenAI Opens Its Newer Model to Free ChatGPT Users
summary: Previously covered on 2026-07-31: OpenAI released GPT-5.

title: USB-C Cable Labels Are Not Worth Trusting
summary: A writer tested a drawer of USB-C cables with a meter and found the printed claims about charging speed and data transfer frequently did not match reality.

title: GitHub's Malware Warnings Now Reach Past npm
summary: GitHub's Advisory Database — the list it uses to warn projects that a piece of third-party code they depend on is malicious — previously covered only npm, the JavaScript package registry.

title: Writing Code Got Cheap. Owning It Didn't.
summary: GitHub's engineering team published a framework for deciding which changes are genuinely cheap now that AI tools write much of the code.
